items.stem: A team wants a foundation-model chatbot to answer using a company's internal policy documents without retraining the model. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that supplies relevant documents at inference time
options.rationale: Correct: RAG injects relevant retrieved content at inference so the model can answer from company data without retraining.

options.text: Deleting the model and writing rules by hand
options.rationale: Hand-written rules forgo the model's capabilities and are not the described approach.

options.text: Training a model from scratch on the entire internet
options.rationale: Training from scratch is unnecessary and far beyond the need.
A chatbot needs prompts to function.

items.explanation: Correct: RAG injects relevant retrieved content at inference so the model can answer from company data without retraining.

items.stem: Which term describes the smaller units of text that a large language model processes?

options.rationale: Correct: LLMs process text as tokens.
Pixels are image units, not text units.
Packets are networking units, not model text units.
Sectors are storage units, unrelated to model text.

items.explanation: Correct: LLMs process text as tokens.

items.stem: Select TWO responsible-AI considerations relevant to deploying a generative-AI application. (Select TWO.)

options.text: Assessing and mitigating bias in outputs
options.rationale: Correct: bias assessment is a core responsible-AI consideration.

options.text: Providing transparency about AI use and limitations
options.rationale: Correct: transparency about AI use and limitations is a responsible-AI consideration.

options.text: Maximizing token count for its own sake
options.rationale: Inflating tokens is not a responsible-AI goal.

options.text: Hiding that AI generated the content from all users

options.rationale: Removing oversight is contrary to responsible AI.

items.explanation: Correct: bias assessment is a core responsible-AI consideration.
